title: Beef & Broccoli Brown Sauce
description: Fresh shiitake gives this glossy beef-and-broccoli wok sauce the savory depth usually supplied by a bottled stir-fry sauce.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

ingredients.name: low-sodium beef broth
ingredients.note: Use plain unsalted beef broth at about 60 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

ingredients.name: unsalted dry drinking sherry
ingredients.note: Use drinking sherry, without added salt.

steps.title: Sweat the shiitake
steps.text: Soften {shi} in {oil} in the HexClad over medium-low heat for 4 minutes until the caps release their juices.

steps.title: Lift the browned bits
steps.text: Stir in {ga} and {gi}, add {sh} and scrape the pan for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Build the brown sauce
steps.text: Add {be}, {a} and {bs}. Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Smooth the base
steps.text: Take off the heat and use an immersion blender to puree the mushrooms completely. Return to the pan, stir in {so} and bring to a simmer.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Fold the brown sauce around cooked thin-sliced beef and crisp-tender fresh broccoli just before serving.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 5 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, replace the sherry with water and halve the ginger. Nutrition counts the full sherry before simmering. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 57 kcal, 1.3 g protein, 7.1 g total carbohydrate, 1.8 g fat, 0.4 g fiber, 128 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 52 kcal, 1.3 g protein, 5.7 g total carbohydrate, 1.8 g fat, 0.4 g fiber, 38 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
